steps.tx: **Immune-related adverse events** irAEs arise from autoimmune breakdown of self-tolerance following CTLA-4, PD-1, or PD-L1 blockade, potentially affecting any organ system. CTLA-4 inhibitors like ipilimumab predominantly trigger enterocolitis and hypophysitis by disinhibiting early T-cell priming in lymph nodes, whereas PD-1 and PD-L1 inhibitors more frequently induce pneumonitis, thyroiditis, and vitiligo by reinvigorating exhausted effector T-cells in peripheral tissues.

left.title: Anti-CTLA-4 Toxicity Profile
points: Onset typically within first 6 to 12 weeks

right.title: Anti-PD-1 / PD-L1 Toxicity Profile
points: Can manifest months to years after initiation

steps.tx: Gastrointestinal toxicity is among the commonest severe presentations requiring early intervention. **Checkpoint inhibitor colitis** presents with profuse watery diarrhoea and mucosal ulceration; grade 2 or higher colitis requires systemic corticosteroids with prednisone 1 to 2 mg/kg daily. Diarrhoea exceeding four stools over baseline represents grade 2, mandating checkpoint inhibitor interruption, infectious stool workup including Clostridioides difficile, and rapid immunosuppression.

nodes.label: Hold IO + Prednisone 1 to 2 mg/kg daily

steps.tx: Failure to improve on corticosteroids within two to three days warrants prompt second-line biologic therapy. **Steroid-refractory** immune colitis failing systemic corticosteroids within 48 to 72 hours requires prompt escalation to anti-TNF antibody infliximab or gut-selective integrin inhibitor vedolizumab. Infliximab 5 mg/kg administered intravenously neutralizes mucosal TNF-alpha, while vedolizumab targets alpha-4-beta-7 integrin to block gut-homing T-lymphocyte trafficking.

left.title: Infliximab (Anti-TNF)
points: 5 mg/kg IV at weeks 0, 2, and 6 as needed
Rapid clinical improvement within 24 to 48 hours
Screen for latent tuberculosis and hepatitis B

right.title: Vedolizumab (Anti-Integrin)
points: No systemic immunosuppression or infection risk
Preferred if history of latent infections or cancer

steps.tx: Pulmonary complications carry significant mortality if recognition is delayed. Immune checkpoint inhibitor **pneumonitis** manifests as dyspnoea, dry cough, and ground-glass opacities, requiring immediate drug interruption, high-dose steroids, and infectious bronchoscopy workup. Grade 2 pneumonitis with mild symptoms requires oral prednisone 1 to 2 mg/kg daily, whereas grade 3 or 4 hypoxia requires intravenous methylprednisolone 2 to 4 mg/kg daily.

steps.tx: Autoimmune endocrine toxicities damage hormone-producing glands and rarely recover endogenous production. Endocrine irAEs including **hypophysitis** and thyroiditis are typically irreversible, requiring long-term hormone replacement with levothyroxine or physiological hydrocortisone without discontinuing immunotherapy. Hypophysitis manifests with frontal headache and central secondary adrenal insufficiency with low ACTH, requiring urgent morning cortisol testing and hydrocortisone replacement.

left.title: Immune Hypophysitis
points: Low ACTH, low TSH, low LH/FSH on endocrine panel

right.title: Immune Thyroiditis
points: Transient hyperthyroid phase followed by permanent hypothyroid
Elevated TSH with low free T4

steps.tx: Hepatic toxicity presents insidiously with laboratory transaminitis. Checkpoint inhibitor-associated hepatitis presents with asymptomatic AST/ALT elevations; steroid-refractory **immune hepatitis** is treated with oral mycophenolate mofetil rather than infliximab. Infliximab carries an FDA black-box warning for hepatotoxicity and is contraindicated. Oral mycophenolate mofetil 500 to 1000 mg twice daily suppresses hepatic T-cell infiltration, monitored until liver enzymes fall below grade 1.

steps.tx: Standardized oncological grading systems categorize severity and direct intervention urgency. **CTCAE**, or Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events, grades irAE severity from grade 1 mild asymptomatic to grade 4 life-threatening and grade 5 death. Grade 1 toxicities generally permit continuing checkpoint blockade under close clinical surveillance, whereas grade 2 mandates holding therapy, and grade 3 or 4 requires immediate hospital admission and high-dose immunosuppression.

steps.tx: Decisions regarding resuming checkpoint blockade after resolution require careful risk-benefit evaluation. Immune checkpoint inhibitor **rechallenge** is generally safe for resolved low-grade toxicities but is permanently contraindicated following severe grade 4 irAEs, especially myocarditis and Stevens-Johnson syndrome. Myocarditis carries up to fifty percent mortality, presenting with elevated troponin, conduction blocks, and ventricular arrhythmias requiring immediate high-dose pulse methylprednisolone.
